cosy-lesson.title: "Knowledge isn't free. You have to pay attention.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Knowledge – information, skills, and deep understanding acquired through systematic study or experience.

p.em: Example: Getting raw facts online is easy, but converting them into real, structured knowledge requires effort.

cosy-blockquote.p: Attention – notice taken of someone or something; active, focused mental concentration.

p.em: Example: To understand a complex mathematical equation, you must pay undivided attention to the explanation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passive – accepting, watching, or allowing what happens without active response, effort, or interaction.

p.em: Example: Staring at language-learning videos passively will never help you speak fluently.

cosy-blockquote.p: Concentration – the action or power of focusing all your attention and mental energy on one narrow task.

p.em: Example: The constant noise of construction outside completely destroyed her deep concentration.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distraction – a thing that prevents someone from giving their full attention or focus to something else.

p.em: Example: A smartphone notification is a highly dangerous distraction when you are trying to study.

cosy-blockquote.p: To retain – to continue to have, keep, or hold possession of something (like vocabulary or facts) in your memory.

p.em: Example: It is incredibly difficult to retain grammatical rules if you never practice them in conversation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Effort – a vigorous, determined, and continuous attempt requiring physical or mental energy.

p.em: Example: Learning a foreign language is not a passive hobby; it requires consistent daily effort.

cosy-blockquote.p: To absorb – to take in, assimilate, and fully understand complex information or ideas.

p.em: Example: He sat quietly in the back row, trying to absorb every word of the professor's lecture.

cosy-blockquote.p: Superficial – existing or occurring only on the surface; shallow, lacking depth or thoroughness.

p.em: Example: Staring at vocabulary flashcards for two minutes gives you only a superficial understanding of the words.

cosy-blockquote.p: Invaluable – extremely useful, precious, or indispensable; having value too great to be measured in money.

p.em: Example: The advice he received from his mentor was invaluable for his scientific career.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What does Richard Feynman mean when he says knowledge isn't free, and what is its true cost?
★ Complete using inversion: 'Seldom do we discover profound truths without active questioning.'

Why does sitting passive in a lecture hall fail to help us to retain information long-term?
★ Do you find yourself sliding into a passive learning state when listening to audio or podcasts?

How does the modern internet reward superficial learning over deep, focused concentration?
★ What is the single biggest distraction that ruins your daily study focus?

Why does the brain need consistent mental effort to to absorb and process complex scientific concepts?
★ What is an invaluable study habit or routine that helps you to retain difficult facts?

How can teachers design lessons that reduce distraction and demand active, physical effort from students?
★ Do you prefer study environments that are completely silent, or do you like some background noise?

Why is an invaluable mentor who forces you to struggle with questions much better than a simple answer?
★ What is the most invaluable piece of learning advice you have received in your life?

How does having a superficial understanding of global issues lead to narrow and biased arguments?
★ How do you personally make sure that your knowledge of your favorite topic is not just shallow and superficial?

Why does a child's natural curiosity make them much better at to absorb new information than an adult?
★ When you study, how do you reward your own effort to stay motivated?

Can we build deep concentration in a world designed around 10-second videos and endless notifications?
★ How long can you maintain absolute concentration before needing a short break?

Is it possible to acquire real knowledge without experiencing any frustration or struggle?
★ If you had to describe your childhood relationship with school study in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: Which modern learning scenario is most likely to help you retain real knowledge? Rank them: - 📖 The Solo Scholar Reading thick physical textbooks in a silent library, making manual summaries, accepting high initial mental effort. - 📱 The Digital Nomad Watching short interactive video lectures, completing gamified quizzes, but facing constant phone distraction. - 👥 The Debate Group Discussing complex theories with peer students in a coffee shop, practicing active speaking, but moving slowly. - 🎓 The Flipped Classroom Studying basic rules passively at home, then spending classroom time solving difficult problems with a mentor.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will allow us to instantly to absorb complex scientific databases, making traditional school study obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if you never had to make any mental effort to acquire knowledge?

Future societies will completely ban short-video algorithms, forcing people to practice long-term concentration. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use smart brain implants to help you completely block daily digital distraction?

In the coming decades, the capacity to pay undivided attention will become the most valuable economic currency. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where human brains are too distracted to create any new invention?

As artificial intelligence advances, human memory will degrade because we no longer need to retain any facts physically. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of personal memory to retain rules?

Future educational systems will completely eliminate passive lectures, designing lessons around a child's active curiosity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think future kids will be more passive learners than today's children?

A future world governed fully by smart technology will leave no space left for the quiet mystery of manual invention. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a computer could perfectly replicate your knowledge, would you still value human study?

Future generations will look back at today's superficial social media news feeds with deep shock and skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about the importance of paying attention to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make it incredibly difficult to protect your child's brain from continuous distraction. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic community that completely guarantees children's safety at the cost of their freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by how invaluable your actual wisdom is rather than your material wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope personal focus will play in your own professional future over the next decade?

One day, being passionately slow and focused on quality will be seen as the single most valuable trait of any worker, making superficial speed obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you feel you need to practice deeper concentration right now?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
